svg.text: One step's copy: 8 values of i for the block's 128 rows, from GPU memory into shared memory, turned round
The number in each cell is the thread that copies it. Each thread reads one float4 (4 floats) and writes it down a column.
the block's rows t, this step's 8 columns i
8 rows i × 132 floats: 128 rows t, then 4 unused
Thread n reads row t = n ÷ 2, values i = 4 × (n mod 2) … +3: one float4 of 16 bytes, the widest read a thread can do.
It writes those 4 values down column t of the piece, one at a time. 256 threads × 4 values = 1,024 = 128 rows t × 8 i.
Why turn it round: at one i, a thread needs its 8 rows t. In x they are 768 floats apart; in the piece they sit side by side,
so it reads them with two float4 instead of eight single reads (Figure 6). The piece of W, W[j][i] for the block's 128
output columns j, is copied the same way. Each piece row is 132 floats long, not 128: run 1's padding, against bank conflicts.
